root_causes.root_cause: RFC-034 D18 write-barrier _confirm_write_visible() in storage.py adds up to 4.4s blocking delay per save call via time.sleep() with _WRITE_BARRIER_DELAYS=(0.1,0.3,1.0,3.0). Called after both save_doc (.json) and save_doc_meta (.meta.json), worst-case is 8.8s for tree path or 4.4s for flat path. On exhaustion, raises PersistenceNotVisibleError(RuntimeError) which crashes the converter child; since RuntimeError maps to converter_child_failed (not in _TERMINAL_CHILD_REASONS), arq retries the entire job (MAX_TRIES=2), doubling total processing time. For the Arabic SLA doc (slow processor due to bilingual/scanned content), this extra latency or forced retry pushed completion to 06:31:28Z -- 3-5 minutes past the scorer's 06:26-06:28 polling cohort -- producing a false ERROR verdict despite eventual success.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/storage.py::_confirm_write_visible -> _WRITE_BARRIER_DELAYS -> PersistenceNotVisibleError; called from save_doc (line 212) and save_doc_meta (line 575)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two complementary fixes: (1) Reduce _WRITE_BARRIER_DELAYS to a less aggressive schedule (e.g., (0.05, 0.1, 0.3) = 0.45s total) since MinIO's read-after-write consistency is typically sub-100ms. (2) Catch PersistenceNotVisibleError in save_doc/save_doc_meta and downgrade to a warning log + metric rather than crashing the child -- the put_object already succeeded, so stat_object flakiness is an observability gap, not data loss. This prevents the costly full-job retry that doubles processing time.

root_causes.root_cause: world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf is a pre-existing converter timeout (ERRORed 3+ consecutive runs per worker.py:54 code comment). The document exceeds CHILD_TIMEOUT (3600s) / JOB_TIMEOUT (3630s) consistently. This is unrelated to the D18 write barrier -- the job never reaches the persistence path. The write barrier's 4.4-8.8s is negligible relative to the 3630s timeout ceiling.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Investigate why this document exceeds the 3630s timeout. Likely candidates: (1) large page count hitting chunked Docling per-chunk overhead, (2) pdf-inspector classifying it as scanned/image_based triggering the 16.5x timeout multiplier (line 329) which exceeds JOB_TIMEOUT causing arq to kill the job before the inner asyncio.timeout fires. If 16.5x * CHILD_TIMEOUT > JOB_TIMEOUT, the inner timeout never triggers and arq's outer kill leaves no clean error status. Cap effective_timeout to JOB_TIMEOUT - CHILD_GRACE_SECONDS.
